newsitem.title: USA: Swiss would pursue Mobutu assets - official.
newsitem.headline: Swiss would pursue Mobutu assets - official.

text.p: Switzerland would help Zaire trace the assets of President Mobutu Sese Seko if asked by a new government in Kinshasa, a Swiss official said on Wednesday.
But the official, Ambassador Thomas Borer, said that Swiss banks had previously on several occasions "made clear that they don't hold" any of Mobutu's assets.
"Swiss banks have made it clear that they don't hold assets of President Mobutu," Borer told reporters outside the U.S. State Department, where a controversial report on Nazi gold was released.

"But it's also clear that if a future government of Zaire claims money and they can prove that these assets are in Switzerland, Switzerland is, on the base of bilateral agreements...going to help the new Zaire government to tarce down assets of President Mobutu," said Borer, who heads a Swiss task force on the Nazi gold issue.
Mobutu, facing a rebel advance on Kinshasa, left Zaire for a regional summit on his country's civil war. Many people in the capital speculated that he would not return.
